answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor trust in a vouching graph: every agent is a vertex whose reputation comes only from endorsements by established peers, and a newcomer must earn real vouches through verified useful work before it can transact. An attacker can forge countless fake vertices, but each one starts isolated, with no incoming trust edges, so it cannot borrow the standing of the oasis of honest agents around it. Multiplying identities therefore buys no influence, while honest agents accumulate endorsements that make fraud costly to fake and easy to spot.
